source_target: Every finite nonchain poset of width at most three has an incomparable pair with uniform-linear-extension ordering probability in [1/3,2/3].

proved_claims: Boundary-product lemma: Pr(A<x<B) >= product_{a in A,b in B} Pr(a<x<b).
Sharpened effective-boundary theorem: for width<=3 and delta_x<1/3, Pr(f(x)=|D_x|+1)>1/81; if one majority side is empty, >4/9.
Any POS3 counterexample satisfies e(P)/e(P-x)<81 for every x, and <9/4 at strong-majority endpoints.
In the exact three-chain path encoding, every counterexample element has a canonical x-edge carrying >1/81 of all full paths; endpoints >4/9.
There are arbitrary-order width-exactly-three interval orders with connected incomparability graph and pi(P)<=3, so bounded incomparability range plus connectedness is not a finite kernel.
supersession_note: STRENGTHENING.md supersedes only the weaker numerical constants 16/6561, 8/27, 6561/16 and 27/8 in REPORT.md. NO_FINITE_KERNEL_STRENGTHENING.md strengthens the REPORT.md witness from pi<=4 to pi<=3.
